Confusable pairs among the phone rules, age and weight thresholds and protection rules, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A02
Every driver is barred from texting or emailing while driving, but a driver under 18 is barred from using a phone at all while moving, apart from a 911 emergency call. [A02]
Why it matters: group phone law; difficulty medium; confusable all-driver ban versus under-18 ban.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A02
The texting ban and the under-18 ban are laws, while advice to use a phone only for emergencies or family contact is a safety reminder rather than a separate legal rule. [A02]
Why it matters: group phone law; confusable law versus advice.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A05
A child under 8 and under 80 pounds needs a weight-appropriate restraint, while the rear-seat rule near an active front air bag covers a child under 5 and under 40 pounds. [A05]
Why it matters: group child restraints; difficulty high; confusable age and weight pairs.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A05
A lap belt alone is allowed for a child under 8 weighing 40 to 80 pounds only when no seat has a lap and shoulder belt for the restraint. [A05]
Why it matters: group child restraints; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A06
Riding in the rear seat is advised for children 12 and under, while riding in an open pickup bed is prohibited by law for children under 16. [A06]
Why it matters: group child safety; confusable advice age versus legal age.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A01
A short nap with caffeine is only a temporary help for fatigue, while the long-trip habit is a stop at least every 2 hours. [A01]
Why it matters: group fatigue; confusable temporary fix versus routine break.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A03
Coffee, a big meal and a cold shower do nothing to sober a drinker; only the passing of time does. [A03]
Why it matters: group alcohol; misconception target.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A04
Air bags never excuse the seat belt, and a vehicle with an automatic shoulder harness still requires the lap belt to be fastened. [A04]
Why it matters: group belts; confusable harness versus lap belt.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A04
The frequent-delivery seat belt exemption applies only if the vehicle stays at or below 20 mph between stops. [A04]
Why it matters: group belt exemptions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A06
A DOT symbol fixed permanently by the manufacturer marks a compliant helmet, while a DOT sticker sold separately or added by the rider does not. [A06]
Why it matters: group helmets; confusable permanent symbol versus loose sticker.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]
